title: A neural circuit for context-dependent multimodal signaling in Drosophila.
source_locator: Results, 'Stationarity is necessary and sufficient to drive vibrations in males'; Fig. 3C-D; Fig. S4C; Table 1; Methods, Optogenetics
quote: Conversely, inducing female walking by optogenetically activating the DNp28 neurons55,56 nearly abolished vibrations (Fig. 3C, D).
mapping_basis: The paper calls the cells DNp28, but Table 1 gives the line as SS01587 (R11H10-p65.AD; VT033947-GAL4.DBD), which driver_lines.csv maps to DNp29 (Namiki 2018; eLife 107450 table); the kit's DNp28 lines are SS01056/SS01589/SS01590 with different hemidrivers, so the explicit genotype was preferred over the label; the paper gives no anatomy to decide.
stimulation: 625 nm red LED, 89 mW/cm2, 5 s stimulation followed by 25 s pause, 30 trials
sensory_condition: freely moving female courted by a wild-type NM91 male in a 44 mm x 1.9 mm chamber on paper; room light off, weak 470 nm illumination
n_flies_note: DNp28-Chrimson+ (retinal-fed) N = 9 pairs; controls DNp28-Gal4+ N = 4, UAS-Chrimson+ N = 5, DNp28-Chrimson- N = 7
notes: Locomotion measured only as body-centroid velocity from top-view tracking (DeepPoseKit on head/thorax/abdomen/wings; no leg tracking), so legs coded yes per PROTOCOL section 3 ('increased locomotion' without leg tracking), confidence medium. Fig. 3C: female velocity rises from ~1 mm/s before light to ~12 mm/s during the 5 s light and returns after offset (the wild-type male follows). Pre-stimulus females were near-stationary (~1 mm/s), so this is initiation/strong increase of locomotion, not only a speed change in already-walking flies. Walking direction is not stated; forward_walking assumed from 'inducing female walking' and the large translational velocity. Fig. S4C legend: 'Inducing female acceleration suppresses vibrations ... and increases the male-female distance.' The paper's own circuit model (Fig. 6) concerns P1a/pC2l, not this DN; no connectome-activation-screen score seen.
